newsitem.title: USA: Conf Board's Fosler sees strong US economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Conf Board's Fosler sees strong US economic growth.

text.p: New York Conference Board Chief Economist Gail Fosler said Tuesday that U.S. economic growth was currently stronger than expected.
"We're entering the year with a good deal more forward momentum than I think most economists had expected," Fosler told a National Economists Club luncheon here.
"We're in another period of acceleration, where the economy is gradually building to some kind of interim cycle peak," Fosler said.
She said that GDP growth in the fourth quarter was surprisingly high.
"Fourth quarter growth is going to turn out to be surprisingly good," Fosler said.
"In my own judgement it's something on about the four-percent range, but it could match the second quarter, depending what happens to inventory," she added.
Fosler said economic growth was "building, not decelerating."
"The economy is growing at above trend rates, and resource restraints on the capacity side are being absorbed and they are already tight on the labor side," she said.
She also warned that inflation was moving higher.
"Inflation, while certainly modest to those of us who cut our teeth on the 1970s, is moving upward aided by higher food and energy prices," she said.
Fosler criticized the tendency to discount increases in food and energy prices and focus solely on the so-called core rate that excludes those two elements.
